title: Acts Chapter 28 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 28 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 28 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 28.

questions.question: In Acts 28, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Paul was bitten by a viper
Paul healed the father of Publius
questions.explanation: Acts 28:1 states that when they escaped, they knew the island was called Melita, which is the first event mentioned in the chapter.

questions.question: What did the barbarous people do for Paul and the others because of the rain and cold?
options: Kindled a fire and received them
questions.correctAnswer: Kindled a fire and received them
questions.explanation: Acts 28:2 says the barbarous people kindled a fire and received everyone because of the rain and cold.

questions.question: What came out of the fire when Paul laid a bundle of sticks on it?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:3 states that a viper came out of the heat when Paul laid sticks on the fire.

questions.question: What did the barbarians think Paul was when they saw the venomous beast hanging on his hand?
options: A murderer who escaped the sea but still must die
questions.correctAnswer: A murderer who escaped the sea but still must die
questions.explanation: Acts 28:4 explains that the barbarians said among themselves that Paul was a murderer who escaped the sea but vengeance would not let him live.

questions.question: What did Paul do with the viper that fastened on his hand?
options: Shook it off into the fire
Held it until it let go
questions.correctAnswer: Shook it off into the fire
questions.explanation: Acts 28:5 states Paul shook off the beast into the fire and felt no harm.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the barbarians after seeing Paul unharmed by the viper?
options: They said he was a god
questions.correctAnswer: They said he was a god
questions.explanation: Acts 28:6 says after watching for a long time and seeing no harm come to Paul, they changed their minds and said he was a god.

questions.question: Who was the chief man of the island that received Paul and his companions?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:7 identifies Publius as the chief man of the island who received them and lodged them courteously.

questions.question: What illness did the father of Publius suffer from?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8 states that the father of Publius was sick of a fever and bloody flux.

questions.question: How did Paul heal the father of Publius?
options: Prayed and laid hands on him
questions.correctAnswer: Prayed and laid hands on him
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8 says Paul prayed and laid his hands on Publius's father and healed him.

questions.question: What happened after Paul healed the father of Publius?
options: Others with diseases came and were healed
questions.correctAnswer: Others with diseases came and were healed
questions.explanation: Acts 28:9 states that others who had diseases on the island came and were healed after the healing of Publius's father.

questions.question: How did the islanders show their gratitude to Paul and his companions when they departed?
options: They honored them with many honors and laded them with necessary things
They gave them gold and silver
They held a feast in their honor
They built a monument for them
questions.correctAnswer: They honored them with many honors and laded them with necessary things
questions.explanation: Acts 28:10 says the islanders honored them with many honors and laded them with necessary things when they departed.

questions.question: From which ship did Paul and his companions depart after three months on the island?
options: A ship of Alexandria with the sign Castor and Pollux
questions.correctAnswer: A ship of Alexandria with the sign Castor and Pollux
questions.explanation: Acts 28:11 states they departed in a ship of Alexandria whose sign was Castor and Pollux.

questions.question: Paul and the others were received courteously by Publius for three days.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:7 states that Publius received them and lodged them three days courteously.

questions.question: The viper that bit Paul came out of the fire where the sticks were kindled.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:3 describes that the viper came out of the heat of the fire where Paul had laid the sticks.

questions.question: Paul was bitten by a lion on the island of Melita.
questions.explanation: The text in Acts 28:3 clearly states Paul was bitten by a viper, not a lion.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 28 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 28 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Paul and his companions stay in Syracuse?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:12 states that they tarried there three days.

questions.question: What does Acts 28:13 promise will happen if someone follows the journey laid out in Acts 28:12?
options: They will be delivered to Caesar
questions.explanation: Following the journey in Acts 28:12 leads to Acts 28:14 where they find brethren.

questions.question: Where did Paul and the brethren desire to stay for seven days?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:14 mentions that they found brethren in Puteoli and were desired to tarry with them seven days.

questions.question: What city did Paul reach after Puteoli according to Acts 28:14?
questions.explanation: After Puteoli, as stated in Acts 28:14, they went toward Rome.

questions.question: What did Paul do when he saw the brethren who came to meet him?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:15 indicates that when Paul saw the brethren, he thanked God and took courage.

questions.question: What did the centurion do with the prisoners upon arriving in Rome?
options: Delivered them to the captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: Delivered them to the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Acts 28:16 states that the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard.

questions.question: Why did Paul call the chief of the Jews together in Rome?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:17 shows that Paul called them together to explain he had committed nothing against their people.

questions.question: What did Paul say was the reason for his imprisonment?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:20 reveals that Paul was bound with a chain for the hope of Israel.

questions.question: What was the response of the Jews when Paul explained his situation?
options: They had received letters against him
questions.explanation: Acts 28:22 illustrates that they wanted to hear what Paul thought, indicating their interest.

questions.question: What did Paul express gratitude for upon seeing the brethren?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:15 shows that Paul thanked God when he saw the brethren who came to meet him.

questions.question: What did the Jews in Rome not receive concerning Paul?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:21 indicates they had not received letters from Judaea concerning Paul.

questions.question: What did Paul do to the father of Publius who was sick?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8 states that Paul entered in, prayed, and laid hands on him, healing him.

questions.question: True or False: Paul had committed crimes against the Jewish people.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:17 shows Paul claimed he had committed nothing against the Jewish people.

questions.question: True or False: The people of Melita showed Paul and his companions little kindness.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:2 states that the barbarous people showed them no little kindness.

questions.question: True or False: Paul was allowed to dwell by himself with a soldier who kept him.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:16 mentions that Paul was suffered to dwell by himself with a soldier, indicating he was under guard but not in chains.

hard.title: Acts Chapter 28 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 28.

questions.question: In Acts 28:23, how long did Paul expound and testify the kingdom of God to those who came to his lodging?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:23 states Paul expounded and testified 'from morning till evening'.

questions.question: According to Acts 28:24, what was the reaction of those who heard Paul’s testimony about Jesus?
options: Some believed and some believed not
questions.correctAnswer: Some believed and some believed not
questions.explanation: Acts 28:24 explicitly says, 'And some believed the things which were spoken, and some believed not.'

questions.question: In Acts 28:25, Paul quotes the Holy Ghost through Esaias the prophet. What did he say about this prophecy?
options: Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers
The prophecy was only partly fulfilled
The prophecy was not relevant anymore
questions.correctAnswer: Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers
questions.explanation: Acts 28:25 records Paul saying, 'Well spake the Holy Ghost by Esaias the prophet unto our fathers'.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'the heart of this people is waxed gross' in Acts 28:27?
options: Their hearts have become calloused or dull
Their hearts are full of joy
Their hearts are soft and repentant
questions.correctAnswer: Their hearts have become calloused or dull
questions.explanation: Acts 28:27 describes the people’s hearts as 'waxed gross,' indicating a dullness or callousness preventing understanding.

questions.question: According to Acts 28:28, to whom is the salvation of God sent?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:28 states, 'the salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles'.

questions.question: How long did Paul dwell in his own hired house in Rome as described in Acts 28:30?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:30 indicates Paul dwelt two whole years in his own hired house.

questions.question: WORD STUDY: What does the Greek word 'ἐξηγήσατο' (exēgēsato) in Acts 28:23 mean?
questions.explanation: 'ἐξηγήσατο' in Acts 28:23 means 'expounded' or 'explained,' referring to Paul's detailed teaching.

questions.question: LITERARY DEVICE: What literary technique is primarily used in Acts 28:26-27 with the phrases 'Hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and not perceive'?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:26-27 uses parallelism, repeating similar sentence structures to emphasize spiritual blindness.

questions.question: CROSS-REFERENCE: Which Old Testament passage is directly quoted and connected to Paul's message in Acts 28:25-27?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:25-27 quotes Isaiah 6:9-10 describing the people's hardened hearts.

questions.question: CROSS-REFERENCE: The theme of salvation being extended to the Gentiles in Acts 28:28 is fulfilled in which New Testament passage?
questions.explanation: Romans 11:11-12 discusses salvation coming to the Gentiles, echoing Acts 28:28.

questions.question: WHAT-COMES-BEFORE: Which event immediately precedes Paul’s calling the chief of the Jews together in Acts 28:17?
options: Paul was delivered to the captain of the guard
Paul was healed from a viper bite
Paul sailed from Melita to Rome
questions.correctAnswer: Paul was delivered to the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Acts 28:16 states the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, preceding Acts 28:17.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in Acts 28:31 where Paul preaches 'with all confidence, no man forbidding him'?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:31 forms an inclusio by framing the chapter with Paul's bold, unhindered preaching.

questions.question: How does Acts 28:4-6 use typology to present Paul’s viper bite and survival?
options: Paul’s survival typifies divine protection and vindication
It typifies the danger of the sea
It typifies the power of the islanders
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s survival typifies divine protection and vindication
questions.explanation: Acts 28:4-6 shows Paul bitten by a viper but unharmed, typifying God's protection over him.

questions.question: Which cultural context is important for understanding the reception of Paul in Melita as described in Acts 28:2 and 28:7-10?
options: The islanders' hospitality despite being 'barbarous' reflects Mediterranean customs
Melita was a major Roman city
The islanders were hostile and rejected Paul
There was no interaction with locals
questions.correctAnswer: The islanders' hospitality despite being 'barbarous' reflects Mediterranean customs
questions.explanation: Acts 28:2 and 28:7-10 describe the islanders’ kindness despite being called 'barbarous,' reflecting regional hospitality traditions.

questions.question: TRUE/FALSE: Acts 28:29 states that after Paul's message, the Jews immediately accepted his teachings without dispute.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:29 says the Jews departed and 'had great reasoning among themselves,' indicating dispute.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 28 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 28 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 28:6 teach about God's power over natural and supernatural phenomena?
options: God demonstrates His power by protecting His servants from harm.
God allows His people to suffer natural consequences of sin.
God is indifferent to the physical dangers believers face.
God only intervenes in spiritual matters, not physical ones.
questions.correctAnswer: God demonstrates His power by protecting His servants from harm.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:6 shows that despite the venomous viper biting Paul, no harm came to him, indicating God's protective power over natural dangers.

questions.question: What doctrine about salvation does Acts 28:28 teach?
options: Salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and they will hear it.
Salvation is exclusive to the Jewish people as God's chosen nation.
Salvation is earned through adherence to the law only.
Salvation is only for those who physically go to Jerusalem.
questions.correctAnswer: Salvation of God is sent unto the Gentiles, and they will hear it.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:28 declares explicitly that God's salvation is now extended to the Gentiles, fulfilling the inclusion of the nations in God's redemptive plan.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding human sin and hardness of heart is taught in Acts 28:27?
options: The hardness of heart prevents people from perceiving and receiving God's message.
Human sin is irrelevant to God's plan of salvation.
God removes all spiritual blindness immediately upon hearing the gospel.
Sin is only a physical problem, not a spiritual one.
questions.correctAnswer: The hardness of heart prevents people from perceiving and receiving God's message.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:27 explains that the people's hearts have become 'waxed gross' and ears dull, causing them not to understand or convert, showing the doctrinal reality of spiritual blindness due to sin.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 28:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:18 notes that Paul was examined and found innocent of death-worthy crimes, demonstrating God's justice in the Roman legal process.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 28:31 specifically demonstrate in Paul's ministry?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:31 highlights Paul preaching and teaching 'with all confidence, no man forbidding him,' demonstrating the divine attribute of boldness enabled by the Spirit.

questions.question: How does Acts 28:16 connect to the broader biblical theme of Christ's kingship and the extension of His kingdom?
options: Paul's arrival in Rome symbolizes the gospel reaching the seat of imperial power, fulfilling the universal scope of Christ's kingdom.
It shows the limitation of Christ's kingdom only to Jewish territories.
It demonstrates that earthly kingdoms will always oppose the gospel.
It is unrelated to the theme of Christ's kingship.
questions.correctAnswer: Paul's arrival in Rome symbolizes the gospel reaching the seat of imperial power, fulfilling the universal scope of Christ's kingdom.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:16 situates Paul in Rome, the empire's center, symbolizing the gospel's advance to the heart of worldly power, aligning with the theme of Christ's universal reign.

questions.question: How does the healing ministry in Acts 28:8–9 prefigure Christ's ministry as depicted in the Gospels?
options: It demonstrates the continuation of Christ's healing power through His apostles.
It contradicts the gospel's emphasis on spiritual healing alone.
It shows that miracles were limited to Christ's earthly ministry.
It suggests that healing was a sign only for Jews.
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates the continuation of Christ's healing power through His apostles.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8–9 shows Paul healing Publius's father and others, reflecting the ongoing presence of Christ's healing power in the apostolic mission.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 28:23 and 28:31 teach about the nature and content of apostolic ministry?
options: The apostolic ministry involves persistent teaching of the kingdom of God and Jesus Christ with confidence and without hindrance.
The apostles only taught in synagogues and avoided Gentile audiences.
The apostolic ministry was secretive and limited to private settings.
The apostles relied on political powers to enforce their message.
questions.correctAnswer: The apostolic ministry involves persistent teaching of the kingdom of God and Jesus Christ with confidence and without hindrance.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:23 describes Paul expounding the kingdom of God from morning to evening, and 28:31 shows him teaching with confidence unhindered, illustrating the relentless and bold nature of apostolic proclamation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 28:26–27 and 28:22 teach about the Jewish reception of the gospel?
options: The Jews knew of the sect but their hearts were hardened, leading to rejection of the gospel despite some curiosity.
The Jews fully embraced the gospel immediately upon hearing it.
The Jews were unaware of the gospel until Paul's arrival in Rome.
The Jews universally persecuted the gospel with no internal debate.
questions.correctAnswer: The Jews knew of the sect but their hearts were hardened, leading to rejection of the gospel despite some curiosity.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:22 shows the Jews knew about the sect yet wanted to hear Paul's views; 28:26–27 quotes Isaiah explaining their hardened hearts preventing repentance and understanding.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 28:17 and 28:19 teach about Paul's legal appeals and his relationship to his Jewish heritage?
options: Paul appeals to Caesar not to accuse his nation but because of opposition from some Jews, showing his continued loyalty to Israel.
Paul completely renounced his Jewish heritage when appealing to Caesar.
Paul appealed to Caesar to destroy the Jewish people.
Paul's appeal was made out of hatred for his own nation.
questions.correctAnswer: Paul appeals to Caesar not to accuse his nation but because of opposition from some Jews, showing his continued loyalty to Israel.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:17–19 shows Paul clarifying that he has done nothing against his people or customs and that his appeal to Caesar was compelled by opposition, not accusation of Israel.

questions.question: What does Acts 28:24–25 teach apologetically about the varied responses to the gospel message?
options: The gospel will be received by some and rejected by others, fulfilling prophecy about hardened hearts.
The gospel is universally accepted by all who hear it.
Disbelief indicates the gospel is false.
Those who reject the gospel have no reason for doing so.
questions.correctAnswer: The gospel will be received by some and rejected by others, fulfilling prophecy about hardened hearts.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:24 notes some believed and some did not; 28:25 cites Isaiah's prophecy about the people's hardened hearts, explaining this mixed response.

questions.question: Skeptics claim that Paul's house arrest in Rome limited his ministry and gospel impact. What does Acts 28:30–31 actually teach?
options: Paul continued preaching and teaching the kingdom of God with all confidence without anyone forbidding him.
Paul ceased all ministry activities during his house arrest.
Paul only ministered to a few select individuals and avoided public teaching.
Paul's ministry was ineffective because of his confinement.
questions.correctAnswer: Paul continued preaching and teaching the kingdom of God with all confidence without anyone forbidding him.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:30–31 states that Paul dwelt in his own hired house and received all who came, preaching and teaching with confidence unhindered.

questions.question: What doctrine about God's providence is illustrated by Acts 28:11–15 in the narrative of Paul's journey to Rome?
options: God sovereignly orchestrates the journey, including favorable winds and fellowship with believers.
Paul's journey was purely accidental with no divine involvement.
God does not intervene in the affairs of travel or human planning.
The journey reflects human effort alone without divine guidance.
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly orchestrates the journey, including favorable winds and fellowship with believers.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:11–15 details Paul's travel with favorable winds and meetings with brethren, indicating God's providential care over his mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God's healing of Publius' father in Acts 28:8?
questions.explanation: Acts 28:8 shows Paul healing Publius' father, reflecting God's merciful compassion toward suffering individuals.

questions.question: What theological significance does the viper incident in Acts 28:3–5 hold regarding God's protection of His messengers?
options: It signifies God's providential protection over His servants even in hostile circumstances.
It indicates that God's protection is only for apostles during sea voyages.
It suggests that danger is always a sign of divine disfavor.
It shows that believers are immune to all physical harm.
questions.correctAnswer: It signifies God's providential protection over His servants even in hostile circumstances.
questions.explanation: Acts 28:3–5 recounts the viper biting Paul but causing no harm, indicating God’s protective providence amid dangers.
